tubular.label: Direct tubular toxicity
tubular.action: Check serum creatinine at baseline and during therapy; avoid other kidney toxins; use drug levels where the label calls for them.

hemodynamic.label: Reduced kidney blood flow
hemodynamic.action: Highest risk with volume depletion, heart failure, liver disease, older age, and use with diuretics, ACE inhibitors or ARBs.

ain.label: Acute interstitial nephritis
ain.action: Can occur at any time during therapy. If kidney function falls, stop the drug and evaluate.

crystal.label: Crystal or stone formation
crystal.action: Keep the patient well hydrated; check creatinine and urine.

glomerular.label: Glomerular injury or proteinuria
glomerular.action: Check urine protein and serum creatinine during therapy.

tma.label: Thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA/HUS)
tma.action: Stop the drug if anemia, low platelets and rising creatinine appear together.

immune.label: Immune-mediated nephritis
immune.action: Monitor serum creatinine during treatment; withhold or stop per the label if nephritis develops.

osmotic.label: Osmotic kidney injury
osmotic.action: Monitor kidney function and urine output; stop if kidney function worsens.

contrast.label: Contrast-associated kidney injury
contrast.action: Check kidney function and hydration before the study; use the lowest dose needed.

renal.label: Kidney injury (mechanism not stated)
renal.action: Monitor serum creatinine during therapy; avoid other kidney toxins.

excluded.ACE inhibitors, ARBs, sacubitril-valsart: Lower glomerular pressure on purpose and protect the kidney long term; a creatinine rise or hemodynamic AKI with volume depletion is covered by their kidney dosing and monitoring, not tagged as nephrotoxic.
excluded.Loop and thiazide diuretics, spironolact: Kidney injury in their labels is from volume depletion, not toxicity.
excluded.Statins, fibrates, gemfibrozil, daptomyc: Kidney injury in their labels is secondary to rhabdomyolysis or a systemic syndrome.
excluded.Tumor lysis (bendamustine, rituximab, ve: Indirect: kidney injury follows tumor lysis or dehydration.
excluded.Antiepileptics and others with DRESS: Nephritis only as part of a multi-organ hypersensitivity syndrome.
excluded.Metformin and its combinations, gadolini: Their kidney warnings are about use IN kidney disease (lactic acidosis, NSF, hypocalcemia, accumulation), not kidney injury; covered by kidney dosing.
excluded.Abemaciclib, exemestane, salmon calciton: Creatinine rise without loss of kidney function, or urine findings only.
excluded.Carboplatin, cefazolin, famciclovir, sit: Label wording too weak, dose-error related, about the bladder, an infection, or a drug interaction; not a direct kidney-injury warning.
excluded.Topiramate, zonisamide: Kidney stones from metabolic acidosis; not kidney injury.
excluded.Aspirin: No kidney-injury warning in the US label on file.

vemurafenib.quote: Renal Failure Renal failure, including acute interstitial nephritis and acute tubular necrosis, can occur with ZELBORAF.

vonoprazan.label: vonoprazan
vonoprazan.quote: Acute Tubulointerstitial Nephritis Acute tubulointerstitial nephritis (TIN) has been reported with VOQUEZNA [see Adverse Reactions (6.1) ] .

voriconazole.label: voriconazole
voriconazole.quote: Renal Toxicity Acute renal failure has been observed in patients undergoing treatment with VFEND.

warfarin.label: warfarin
warfarin.quote: Acute Kidney Injury In patients with altered glomerular integrity or with a history of kidney disease, acute kidney injury may occur with JANTOVEN, possibly in relation to episodes of excessive anticoagulation and hematuria [ see Use in Specific Populations (8.6) ].

zoledronic acid.label: zoledronic-acid
zoledronic acid.quote: Renal Toxicity Administration of zoledronic acid injection 4 mg given as a 5-minute intravenous infusion has been shown to result in an increased risk of renal toxicity, as measured by increases in serum creatinine, which can progress to renal failure.
